clue.text: Bungled attempt to eliminate the supervisor?

definitions.meaning: a dialect term for a botched effort or a miss
read literally, a shot aimed at the boss would get rid of the person in charge

explanation.definitionFit: A dialect phrase for a clumsy miss, punningly also a gun fired at one's manager.

clue.text: One way to get round.

parts.note: a route that skirts a town, and, read on into the next clue, a way of slipping past a guard

explanation.surface: A suggestion of how to get round something, trailing into the next clue's man on guard.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this clue to 2 Down: one way to get round the man on guard is to slip past him.
explanation.definitionFit: A road built around a town centre is the standard way of avoiding going through it.

clue.text: … the man on guard

parts.note: a soldier posted to keep watch, continuing the previous clue's idea of getting round someone

explanation.surface: The figure to be got round in the previous clue: a guard on duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A soldier stationed to watch a gate or post is the classic guard figure.

clue.text: It's our turn to be a petitioner

indicators.note: a turn here is a twist of the letters, so the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone announces it is their turn to make a plea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges the six letters of IT'S OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooer asks for a hand in marriage, and anyone making a request of a court or king is a petitioner too.

clue.text: Brilliant hunter on the run from Artemis?

definitions.text: Brilliant hunter on the run from Artemis?

parts.words: Brilliant hunter on the run from Artemis?
parts.note: the mythical hunter killed by the goddess Artemis became a bright constellation, and 'on the run' hints at belting away

explanation.surface: A dazzling huntsman flees the Greek goddess of the hunt.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Orion the hunter was slain by Artemis and set among the stars; three bright stars form the girdle of his constellation, and 'on the run' plays on belting along.
explanation.definitionFit: Three brilliant stars in a row mark the waist of the hunter constellation.

clue.text: Rash selection for an international match

definitions.text: Rash selection for an international match

parts.words: Rash selection for an international match
parts.note: a player picked for a national side wins a cap, so an unwise pick would be a crazy cap

explanation.surface: Selectors make a hasty pick for an international fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: A player chosen for his country is said to win a cap; a rash choice would be a 'mad cap', which is also a word for a reckless person.
explanation.definitionFit: A reckless, impulsive person or act is described with this word, split here as a crazy selection.

clue.text: A vessel so suitable for a Corinthian capital

parts.note: a can is a metal container
thus means so, in that way

explanation.surface: A container is described as just right for decorating a classical column.
explanation.walkthrough: Corinthian columns have capitals carved with leaves of this plant, so it is fitting decoration for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Stylised leaves of this Mediterranean plant are the carved ornament on Corinthian column tops.

clue.text: Cheers for a double feature

indicators.note: a double gives two copies, so the facial part is written twice

parts.note: the chin is a feature of the face

explanation.surface: Applause greets a cinema showing two films.
explanation.walkthrough: A double chin is also a double feature, punning on the cinema programme.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal toast said when raising glasses.

clue.text: Renting property at Peterhead is so delightful

parts.note: the head of Peter is its first letter, P (Peterhead is also a Scottish port)
leasing is letting out property for rent

explanation.surface: Letting houses in the Scottish fishing town of Peterhead proves very agreeable.
explanation.walkthrough: Peterhead is a port in north-east Scotland, but here it is split as 'Peter head', the letter P, placed at the front of LEASING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives pleasure is agreeable, charming or delightful.

clue.text: Small vessel sound in a frightful state

indicators.note: sound tells us the word for being frightened is heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: panicking means in a state of fright

explanation.surface: A tiny boat is in good shape despite a terrible situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like 'in good condition' but signals that PANICKING said out loud gives the word for a small metal cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A small metal drinking cup or pan, a little container.

clue.text: Born in bed at Whitstable, say

definitions.meaning: belonging to a place by birth
Whitstable, a Kent seaside town, is famous for oysters raised in beds there, known by this name

explanation.surface: Someone was born in a bed in a Kent seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitstable is a town on the Kent coast famous for its oysters; oysters bred in British beds are called natives.
explanation.definitionFit: Belonging to a place by birth; also the trade word for a home-bred oyster.

clue.text: Theological college touchy about Beethoven's birthplace

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the word for touchy goes around the city

parts.note: sore means touchy, resentful
Beethoven was born in Bonn, in Germany

explanation.surface: A divinity college is sensitive about the city where Beethoven was born.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paris university began in the 13th century as a college for theology students.

clue.text: Keeps resolutely to backwood areas

explanation.definitionFit: One verb for firm adherence, and the slang name for remote countryside far from towns.

clue.text: Such is sponsorship on television

parts.note: a sponsor's message shown between programmes is a paid advert

explanation.surface: A remark that TV sponsorship is a business matter.
explanation.definitionFit: An advert on TV is a paid break, and sponsorship is a business matter.

clue.text: Pardon for sailor with the right answer

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
a solution is the correct answer

explanation.surface: A sailor is pardoned for giving the correct reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal forgiveness, especially of sins by a priest, is a pardon.

clue.text: Hit and run in carefree fashion

parts.note: to slap is to hit
to dash is to run

explanation.surface: Someone strikes and flees without a care.
explanation.definitionFit: Done hastily and carelessly, without attention to detail.

clue.text: Fragile container

parts.note: the thin brittle casing a bird's embryo grows inside

explanation.surface: A delicate box or holder.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin brittle casing laid by a hen is a natural, easily broken package.

clue.text: Place of honour mostly and outstandingly good; capital in fact!

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: honor is the American spelling of honour
a lulu is an outstanding thing or person

explanation.surface: A city's place of honour is mainly and remarkably good, being a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Use the American spelling HONOR; 'mostly' drops its last letter, giving HONO. Add LULU, slang for something outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The chief city of Hawaii is its state capital.

clue.text: Supporters of Elia at the butcher's

parts.note: legs support a body
Elia was the pen name of the essayist Charles Lamb

explanation.surface: The legs of an essayist turn up in a meat shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote his Essays of Elia under that pen name, so Elia stands for LAMB.
explanation.definitionFit: Joints of mutton from young sheep sold by meat traders.

clue.text: Playfully asinine he doesn't imbibe in a time of prosperity

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a boom is a period of economic growth
TT, teetotal, describes one who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller behaves foolishly during good economic times.
explanation.walkthrough: The weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream is given an ass's head, so he is playfully 'asinine'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic weaver is literally turned into an ass by Puck.

clue.text: Beginner has nothing against being in Nice

indicators.note: being in shows the two short pieces sit inside the town name

parts.note: O is nothing, zero
V, versus, means against

explanation.surface: A newcomer opposes nothing while on the French Riviera.
explanation.definitionFit: A newcomer or learner is new to an activity.

clue.text: Ordered decree to grow less

indicators.note: ordered here means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A decree is issued commanding something to diminish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' rearranges the six letters of DECREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back or diminish, as floodwaters do.

clue.text: Falstaff's troubleshooter

parts.note: one of Falstaff's swaggering cronies in Shakespeare shares his name with a handgun, a shooter that brings trouble

explanation.surface: A fixer employed by Shakespeare's fat knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Falstaff's companion in Henry IV and Henry V is named after a handgun, punning on 'trouble-shooter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handgun is a shooter, and one of Falstaff's companions bears its name.

clue.text: Oily preservative found by bespectacled cardinal in a Greek island

indicators.note: in tells us the spectacled compass point goes inside the island

parts.note: Crete is a Greek island
a cardinal point, S for south, wearing spectacles drawn as two O's either side

explanation.surface: A wood preservative is found by a cardinal in glasses on Crete.
explanation.walkthrough: The cardinal is a compass point, S, not a churchman; spectacles are drawn as OO, so S wearing them is OSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar-derived oil painted on fences to stop rot.

clue.text: Way open for a scene of action

parts.note: a venue is where an event takes place

explanation.surface: A path is cleared to reach the place where events happen.
explanation.definitionFit: A broad tree-lined road, or figuratively an approach open to someone.

clue.text: Harangue of help in retrospect to a native community

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a community of native people

explanation.surface: A rant about providing aid, looking back, to an indigenous people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' sounds like the speaker looking back on events, but it is the signal to read the word for help from right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A long bitter verbal attack is a tirade or rant.

clue.text: I give more than a passing glance, but it doesn't mean anything

definitions.text: I give more than a passing glance
definitions.meaning: read literally, the speaker devotes their whole gaze
an old slang phrase for nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone looks closely but finds it meaningless.
explanation.definitionFit: Dated British slang exclamation for nonsense or humbug, read literally as giving one's full gaze.
